items.stem: A Lambda function needs to read from a DynamoDB table. What is the recommended way to grant it access?

options.text: Embed an access key and secret in the function code
options.rationale: Hardcoding long-term credentials is insecure and discouraged.

options.text: Attach an IAM execution role with least-privilege permissions
options.rationale: Correct: a Lambda execution role grants temporary, scoped credentials following least privilege.
Public access violates least privilege and security best practice.

options.text: Store the key in an environment variable in plaintext

items.explanation: Correct: a Lambda execution role grants temporary, scoped credentials following least privilege.

items.stem: Which deployment strategy routes traffic to a new environment and allows instant rollback by switching back?

options.rationale: All-at-once has no parallel environment to roll back to instantly.
Correct: blue/green runs a new (green) environment alongside the old (blue) and switches traffic, enabling fast rollback.
That is not an AWS deployment strategy.

options.text: Deleting and recreating the stack each time
options.rationale: That causes downtime and is not a rollback strategy.

items.explanation: Correct: blue/green runs a new (green) environment alongside the old (blue) and switches traffic, enabling fast rollback.

items.stem: Which TWO AWS services are most appropriate for decoupling components of an event-driven application? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: SQS queues decouple producers and consumers.
Correct: SNS enables pub/sub fan-out to decouple components.
Security groups are network firewalls, not decoupling services.
IAM manages access, not component decoupling.
Route 53 is DNS, not a decoupling service.
